_what_this_is: A ready-to-enable SessionStart hook. NOT installed: enabling it changes
how every future Claude session in this project begins, which is a
change to your environment rather than to the app, so it is yours to
turn on. Install with:  powershell -NoProfile -File tools\install-hooks.ps1 -SessionStart
WHAT IT DOES: runs tools/status.py and puts its output at the top of
every new session's context -- the last GATE line with its role= tag,
the live gate score out of five, the git tags, which files are yours
and must not be written, how much of the Director migration is done,
and whether anything is running right now.
WHY: what currently carries between sessions is RULES.md (579 lines)
and CLAUDE.md (~3000 lines), both written by hand and both re-read by
an assistant whose context has just been compacted. That does not work,
and there is direct evidence: rewriting RULES.md I dropped six of my
own rules, three of which described damage done that same day.
Fable's recommendation, reviewing this codebase on 2026-10-15: the
artifact that survives compaction is the one that is SMALL, STRUCTURED
and REGENERATED BY A SCRIPT. Prose cannot be kept honest; a script that
reads the logs, the tags and the files can.
The three claims this project has got wrong by remembering instead of
reading were '17 seconds to READY' (a harness log line, reported as
your bench), 'the arcade modes are hiding your holes' (invented), and
'ready' (from one good run). All three are things status.py prints
correctly from evidence.
